output.best_reason: Version A balances voice, tension and fact delivery best. Félix's bitter, self-aware tone is consistent throughout, and the timings arrive as answers to Matthey's questions rather than as a list. The repeater detail ("I think I did not want to know what they meant") and the closing point that he was alone directly under the atelier build dread without overstating it. E is close behind, with the sharpest wit and a strong closing beat ("Clear. Yes. That is what frightens me"), but it leans on meta-jokes and makes its clues a little too explicit. B has vivid, memorable lines and a moving ending, but it repeats its tics ("I'm the heir," "I talk when I'm frightened") and the watch timings. C has good period texture (Odile, Vauthier, the family tree), but Matthey's "Do you see how that looks?" style of questioning slides into repetition. D opens with the most evocative fragments, yet its voice is the most generic, it restates facts (the piano appears twice), and it ends on a flat note with little tension.
